subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated `before_persistence_write` hook for durable state changes, or represent durable-write policy through existing/enriched tool and provenance contracts instead?
rationale: This choice defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what plugins may see, whether they can block or mutate writes, and how hook failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Fold context into existing hooks
options.body: Extend `before_tool_call` and related provenance/read-time APIs instead of adding a new hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to provenance architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as a dependency of the persistent-state provenance work until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage after maintainer/security review.
